# Shared recovery contract

Use this contract for enabled-memory recovery, upgrades and handover. Follow the instance's approved ownership, source permissions and backup policy.

1. Inventory authoritative Markdown/history/evidence, exact runtime/helper versions, private configuration, frozen cases, selected capabilities and jobs. Distinguish rebuildable SQLite/caches from irreplaceable configuration or imports.
2. Compare baseline, current and incoming managed-file hashes. A customization needs an explicit merge; missing baseline means unknown ownership. Preserve original writing, protected principles, pending proposals and local choices, including absent configuration keys.
3. Capture a consistent verified head and retain the previous package/instruction versions. A local copy is not proof an off-machine backup completed. Report missing recovery dependencies and source ranges honestly.
4. Restore and test in an isolated copy with production writer configuration disabled and live jobs/external mutations unavailable. Verify source bytes, current records, revisions, provenance, graph references, historical answers and pending checkpoints; rebuild SQLite from Markdown.
5. Before cutover, reconcile changes since the baseline, stop conflicting old execution and verify exactly one designated writer. New packages or files do not enable schedules, sources or learned policy automatically.
6. Verify the actual writer receipt and current projections after cutover. Keep failed publication/pending sync distinguishable from an accepted semantic write.
7. Rehearse rollback after creating later decisions, captures and checkpoints. Restore prior instructions/code or append authorized corrective revisions while retaining the full current history. Never overwrite new accepted writes with an old store snapshot or replay completed external actions.
8. Keep private configuration, credentials, raw imports and machine paths out of public distributions. Recovery exports, completed backups and tested restores are separate dated states. Use the instance's authorized destination; do not infer upload, deletion or retention authority.
